segments.text: Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᎩ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᎥᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᎦᏔᎲ ᎬᏗ, ᏍᎩᏭ ᎢᎦ,
segments.translation: I’ve never heard it. I’m just familiar with using it, that’s all.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏃ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎲ Ꮭ'ᏛᎮ ᎦᏳᏅ,Ꮦ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏚᏙᎥ’Ᏺ y’know ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: That’s all they told me. They didn’t know the English names.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Boy, ᎮᎾ, … ᎯᎢᏴ’Ᏺ ᎮᎾ, Ꮲ ᏂᎦᏘ, ᏙᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ, … ᎾᎮᎾ, ᎡᏥ Ꮎ ᏛᎦᏏᏁᎬ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ “ᎯᎢᎾ ᎬᎿᎨ ᎤᏰᎬ ᎠᏭ” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᏙᏳ, ᏩᎩᎪᎲ “ᏙᏳ,--gah, ᏯᏩᎵ,ᏏᏅᏍᏛ,” ᏕᏥᎦᏂᎲ “‘Ꮩ ᏂᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂ,?” ᎠᏪᎵᎲ ᎩᎳ, ᎪᎨᏱ … Ꮩ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏛᏅ -- huh uh! ᏧᏥᎸᏅ’Ꭱ Ꮷ-ᏧᏥᎸᏅ’Ꮓ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏚᏯ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᏂ,ᏓᏛᏅ … ᏙᏳ, ᏂᎨᎵᏙᎵᏒ ᏕᏥᎦᏂᎲ ᎪᎳ, ᏃᏭ ᏗᏢ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ ᎦᎵᏬᎬ ᎬᎿᎨᎢ ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.translation: Boy, it’s about this tall, ain’t it? Mom, she was backing up in her car, “There’s some of that black plant growing back there,” she told me. I went and saw it. I thought, “If I take care of it,” to see what happens in the spring. It produced berries – huh uh! That’s right, it bloomed. When it bloomed, then those bean-like things grew on it. Every time I went there, I’d take a look at it, but when it became winter, it started dying. It turned real black.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ--ᎾᎾ ᏕᏍᏓᏛᏏᏗᏒ Ꮎ ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ, Ꭰ,Ꮵ,ᎩᎵ,’Ꮫ ᏥᏓᏗᎰ Ꮭ ᎢᎸ-- ᏙᎲ? Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏍᏓᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏱᎩ, Ꮳ,ᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎸ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎪᏍᏗ, ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩ,Ꮧ, Ꮎ Ꮳ-ᏣᎪᎲ ᏱᎩ?
segments.translation: How about when we were growing up, us Cherokees, we talked about monsters, ain’t it? Have you all ever noticed or been scared by anything before like that? You haven’t seen anything?

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎠᎩᎪᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, Ꮎ ᏦᏥᏁᎸ ᎾᎥ ᏣᏅ,Ꮨ Ꮎ ᎤᏪᏴ ᏥᏙᏥᏁᎸ ᎥᎾ … Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏥᎪᎥ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎰ ᎢᎾ ᏱᎦᏘ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎬᎿᎨᎢ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎬ ᏧᎿᎷᏏᏗᏒ ᎦᏅᏅ … ᏓᏳᎴᏫᏍᏔᏅ Ꮶ-ᏦᎨᏅᏒ ᏗᏢ, ᏥᏓ--ᏥᏓᏳᎦ,ᏔᏅ ᎣᎩᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏂᎦᏓ, Ꮩ--Ꮎ ᏕᎦᏂᏝᏅ box ᏥᏙᎩᎲ ᏥᏙᎩ--ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏥᏙᎩᏞᏒ(1:02:24) Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᏥᎪᎥ ᏍᏊ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎦᏥᎪᎥ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎦᎸᎳ,Ꮧ, ᏗᏢ, ᏥᏭᎿᎷᏒ
segments.translation: One time, I saw something where we lived. You know, near the water where we lived. I don’t know what it was, what I saw, but I remember it. It was tall and black all over. It was crossing the road. It stopped and it looked toward our house. It scared all of us. On all the beds we put boxes around and got underneath. I don’t know what it was. I have never seen something like that since. It went up the hill.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Was it heading into the woods?

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Was it a person…?

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.translation: It was walking.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: It had two legs?

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.text: ᎥᎥ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ,--Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ … Ꮟ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎰ ᏯᏩᏓᏅ,ᏖᏝ, ᎣᏍᏓ,
segments.translation: Yeah. I still don’t know what it was. I still remember, when I think about it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Was it tall?

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.text: ᎥᎥ “’Ꮩ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎤᏍᏗ, ᎨᎰ?” ᎨᎵᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ
segments.translation: Yeah. Sometimes I wonder what it was.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: You might’ve seen Bigfoot.

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏦᎩᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎸ'ᎡᏲ ᏥᏬᎦᏗᏍᎦᏢᏅ
segments.translation: I don’t know what it was. It scared all of us, though. We went and hid.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎮᎾ ᏃᏭ ᎦᏂᏟ ᎭᏫᏂ, ᏗᏢ, ᎢᏥ--ᏫᏥᏄᏴᏞ
segments.translation: You all went and hid under the beds.

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.translation: (laughter)

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.text: Ꭿ’Ꭱ ᎾᎯᏳ’Ᏺ ᎣᏂ ᎦᏥᎪᎥ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎠᏯ,
segments.translation: That’s the last time I have seen anything.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏂᎯᎾ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩ,Ꮧ, ᏣᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏱᎩ,?
segments.translation: And how about you, you never noticed anything strange?

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: One time, you know the Blackbirds?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: The ones on the hill?

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.text: ᎦᏚᏏ ᏗᏁᎯ, ᎤᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᏞᎦ, ᏦᎦᏁᎳ,Ꮫ Ꮶ--ᏦᎦᏉᏁᎸ ᎮᎾ, ᏃᏭ ᎠᏩᏛᏒ Ꮎ--Ꮎ ᎦᏚᏏ ᏗᏢ, ᏥᎦᏗᎲ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏬᎩᎷᏨ “ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏓᎦᏥᏍᏓᏩᏕᏏ,” Ꮎ ᎠᎩᏚᏥ, “ᎨᏓᎵ ᏗᏢ, ᏓᎦᏥᏍᏓᏩᏕᏏ,” -- ᎠᎦᏍᎬ’Ꮕ, --- “ᏫᏍᏚᎲᎩ, … Ꮎ … ᏫᏍᏚ--ᏫᏍᏚᎲ--ᏫᏍᏚᏅᏅᎢ!” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ, Ꮎ ᎠᏐᏴ Ꮎ anyway, ᏃᏭ ᏬᎩᎶᏒ ᎠᏩᏠᏒ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ Ꮻ! ᎠᏩᏅᎬ’Ꮕ, ᎠᎦᏍᎬ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ’Ꮫ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏫᎾᏮᏂ,Ꮧ *ᎠᎭᏂ,* ᎾᏅ ᏄᏅᏃ ᏥᏙᎬ’Ꮫ “Ꭽ!” ᎦᏗᎲ “ᏓᎬᏍᏕᎸᎯ’Ꭸ?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ’Ꮫ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ! I said, “Ooh wee!” ᏃᏭ ᏥᏓᎩᏲᏒ’Ꮫ Ꮎ … ᎠᏐᏴ ᏩᏩᏣᏅ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ…
segments.translation: Yeah, they live up on the hill. We lived up there for a while, when the house that we grew up in burned. The hill that I’m talking about, we lived there. “I’m going to go with my uncle and them,” [I thought] “I’m going to go with them down the hill.” And it was raining. -- “Go shut the gate,” he told me. Anyway, we went through, I got off to close it. Oh wee! I was in a hurry, and I was having a hard time with the rain. I couldn’t fix it like the way they had it, I was just standing there, “Haw!” I was saying. Something said, “Can I help you?” – I said, “Ooh wee!” I dropped the gate and I went and got back in the wagon. I don’t know what happened.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: No one was there?

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: No!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: And it said it in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: (laughter)

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.text: ᏧᏪᏘ’Ꮫ ᏓᏓᏁᎸ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏙᎲ? ᎤᎾᎾ
segments.translation: There were old houses there, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: Yeah, those… What do you call Blackbird?

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: Sgwalisdi

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Sgwalisdi

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.text: ᎠᎢ ᏗᏢ, ᎠᏂᏁᎸ ᏥᏳᎪ,Ꮧ ᎧᏝᏛ ᏗᏢ, ᎠᎭ,Ꮒ ᏗᏢ, ᏫᎦᏅᏅ ᎠᏯ, ᏦᏤᎲ ᏗᏢ, ᎤᎾ ᎮᎾ, ᏗᏢ, ᎨᎲ ᎾᏅ ᏩᎧ, ᏚᏂᏱ,Ꮫ Ꮎ … ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, … ᏍᎩᏃ ᏥᏍᏚᎲᏍᎬ ᏍᎩ ᎾᎩᏪᏎᎸ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎡᎳᏗ, ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ, ᏱᏭᎵ,ᏍᏚᏅ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏃᏭ ᎠᏩ--ᎠᏩ--ᎠᏩ,--ᏩᏩᏣᏅ’Ꮓ “’Ꮩ’ᎠᏭ?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “Ꭽ! Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ’Ꮫ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏃᏭ Ꮎ ᎠᎩᏚᏥ, “cat…ᏪᏏ cat,” y’know? “Scaredy Cat” ᎠᏗᎲ
segments.translation: They lived up on the hill, but our road went the other way. And that way, the white people had cows in a fence. When it said that to me while I was shutting the gate, I just dropped it. I don’t know what happened. When I got back in the wagon, “What’s wrong?” they said. “Haw! Nothing,” I told them. Then my uncle said, “Wes(a)”. Yknow, like “scaredy cat.”

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That would really scare you, if somebody spoke, and no one was there.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.text: Yeah. ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ’Ꮕ, ᎾᏮᏂ,Ꮧ … … Ꮎ ᎦᏚ -- “ᏓᎬᏍᏕᎸᎯ’Ꭸ?” ᎤᏛᏅ’Ꮫ Boy, ᏩᏩᏓᏂᏴᏛᏅ’Ꮓ
segments.translation: Yeah, I really couldn’t put the gate right. [putting the wire over the fence.] “Can I help you?” it said. Boy, I took off running!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: You didn’t answer him? You just ran.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: I just took off running, I didn’t say anything.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I wonder how funny it was to him.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: (laughter)

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Boy ᎪᎯᎩ ᎬᏪᏙᎸ ᎢᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᎦᏚᏏ, ᎣᎦᎾ,’Ꭷ ᏥᎦᏁᎸ ᏃᏭᎴ…
segments.translation: Boy, it’s been a long time since I’ve been over there on the hill. Where Ogan(a) lived and…

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: Dom

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Dom. He used to live there, too.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: He lived there last.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎣᏂ? ᎾᏅ ᏐᎢ, … …'Ꮩ ᏚᏙᎡ? ᏣᏂ,Ꭸ ᏚᏙᎥ?
segments.translation: He lived there last? And then the other one…what was their name? Was it John?

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: John Stayathome

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Yeah. ᎪᎯᎩ ᎬᏪᏙᎸ ᎢᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᎦᏚᏏ,
segments.translation: Yeah. It’s been a while since I’ve been there on the hill.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’ᎡᏲ ᏓᎻ, ᏥᎨᏒ ᏍᎩᏛ ᎣᎩᏃᏎᎲ “’ᏙᏅ, ᏫᏁᎵ--ᏫᏁᎵ,--ᏫᏁᎵ,--ᏫᏁᎸᏅᎾ, ᎢᎾ ᏗᏢ,? –'ᏙᏅ, ᏗᏣᏓᏅᏎ?” ᏦᏦᎮᎸ’Ꮫ “Ꮡ! ᎠᏂᏥ,ᎩᎵ, ᎬᎩ,ᏖᏍᏔᏁ!” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎭᏗ’ᏴᎢ!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ’Ꮫ -- “ᎥᎥ! Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎠᏟᏍᏓ, ᏂᎨᎲᎾ, ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏕᎪᏛ’Ꮫ” ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.translation: The late Dom, he used to tell us. “Why aren’t you living up there? Why did you move?” We told him. “Whoo! The booger’s ran me off!” he said. “No, that’s not true!” I told him. – “uh huh! There’s no gas in the stove, but they were burning,” he said.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Huh.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.text: ᏙᏱ, ᏗᏢ ᏥᎦᏅ,Ꭺ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ? Ꮭ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎠᏂ,ᏒᏍᎨ ᏍᏊ ᎯᎳ ᏳᏴᏜ, ᎢᎾ’Ꮫ ᏍᎩᎾ, “ᎪᎱᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᏃᏭ, ᏧᏓᏃᏴᏟᏍᏗ, ᎠᏪᎵᏒ’Ꮫ” ᏣᏗᎲ “Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏯᏯ’Ꭱ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏙᏳ,’Ꮓ ᏍᎩᏛ ᎬᎩ,ᏢᏗᏍᏔᏅ ᏃᏭ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᏩᎩᎶᏒ” ᏧᏛᏅ, ᎮᎾ,
segments.translation: He used to sleep outside. He never slept inside. Even if it was real cold. “I thought I heard something make noise inside, but there’d be nobody in there,” he said. “That’s what scared me off. I never went back over there,” he said.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎠᏯ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ'Ᏺ ᏙᏳ, ᎠᏯ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᏯᏩᏓᏂᏱ, ᏙᎲ, ᎬᏲᏕᏙᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, …well uh ᎢᎩ--ᎢᎩᏂᏍᏆᏗᏓ, ᏃᏭ, ᏭᏟᏍᏗ,--ᏭᏟᏍᏗᏭ ᏂᎬᏫ,ᏍᏗ, ᎦᎶᎯ, … Ꮟ ᏂᎩᏍᏆᏛᎾ, ᏓᏍᏛᏯᏛᏛᏂ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎮᎵ Ꮒ,ᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂ, ᎯᎾ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏓ, ᎯᎸᏍᎩ, ᏫᎾᏕᏘᏴᎲ ᏱᎩ,? ᏍᎩᎦᏚ ᏫᎾᏕᏘᏴᎲ, 'Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏕᏍᏗ, ᎮᎵ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏓ,?
segments.translation: That would be scary. I would probably run off, too! If something [like that] was bothering me. We’re about to finish, already. It seems like it went by fast. Before we finish, I’m going to ask you all this. What do you all think is going to happen to this Cherokee language in the future? Like, 15 years in the future. What will the Cherokee language be like?

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎢᏳᎾ,ᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᎨᎵ ᎠᏯ, Ꮟ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎲᏭ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᏧᏂᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏍᏊ ᏯᏂᏬᏂᎯ, Ꮟ ᏓᏁᏲᎲᏍᎬ’Ꮽ,
segments.translation: If they learn it well, I think, they will still be talking. Also, their parents are talking and teaching their kids.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: You think that it can be spoken a little longer?

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.text: Yeah, ᎤᏠᏱ, … ᏙᏳ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏳᎾ,ᏚᎵ ᎤᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ ᏛᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎢ, ᏍᎩᏃ … ᎨᎵᎲ ᎠᏯ, ᏂᏗᏕᏲᏅᎾ, ᏱᎩ, Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓ, ᏍᎩᎾ,-- Ꮟ ᎢᏓᎢᏭ ᏕᏓᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏂᏓ, ᎾᏅ ᎠᏯ, ᎤᏓᏂᎳᎨᏍᏗ, ᎠᏧᏣ, Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏥᏰᏲᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎾᏃ … ᏍᏓᏱ’ᏛᎮ ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏮᏌ, ᎨᎲ ᏥᏣᎳᎩ, ᎾᏅ, ᎤᏂᏙᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᎫᏌ, ᎣᏤᏙᎵᏙᎲ ᎯᎢ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, … ᎤᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏂᏥᏪᎲ Ꮭ--Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎠᎩᏁᏟᏴᏍᏗ, ᏱᎩ, … “English, English,” ᏣᏬᎮᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎤᏕᎳᎰᎯᏍᏍᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ, y’know … ᏂᏥᏪᎲ ᏥᏃᎮᎲ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎯᎢ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎬᏫ,
segments.translation: Yeah, I’m the same. If they really want to learn, they’re going to learn. I think, if we don’t teach it, then nothing can happen. I think if we keep going on teaching it, then it can still be good. That one, my eldest son, I never taught him. I should have worked hard because I was the Cherokee in the house, and their dad was Creek. We moved around a lot. Nowadays, he knows what I’m saying. I don’t have to change anything. He used to say, “English, English,” to me. So, he would know what I was saying. Today, he doesn’t say that.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: 16)Mike: You talk to him all in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.text: Yeah. ᏥᎨᏳ: Yeah. ᏣᎳᎩᎭ, ᏱᎪᎵ,Ꭶ, y’know ᏯᎩ,ᏛᏛᎲᏅ, ᏍᏊ ᎾᏅ Ꮣ--ᏗᎬᎩᎵᏏ, ᏥᏓᏝᏃᎮᏗ,(1:09:17) ᏍᏊ ᎤᏅ,Ꮤ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏄᏪᏍᏗ, yeah, ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏙᏳ, ᏳᎾ,ᏚᎵ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᎦᏴᎵᎨᎢ ᎠᎴ ᎯᎢ, ᏗᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎩ, ᎠᎭ,Ꮒ, ᏗᏢ, ᏙᏳ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏳᎾ,--ᏳᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎠ, ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓ ᎮᎾ, ᎨᎵ ᏃᏭ
segments.translation: Yeah. He can understand all of it. And he’ll ask me stuff, too. I talk to my grandkids, too. Since he knows what to say. If they really want to learn, the parents, and the students over here. If they learn it well, the language will stay.

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.text: ᎠᏯ’Ꮕ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᎩᎧᎭ ᏧᏍᏗᎬ “ᎦᏛᎩᏍᎬᏭ ᏂᎯ, ᎯᏬᏂᎯ, ᎮᎾ,(1:09:45) my granny,” ᏣᏬᎮᎲ “ᏣᏩᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ” ᏣᏬᎮᎲ … Ꮭ’Ᏺ ᎣᏍᏓ,’Ᏺ ᏱᎦᏬᏂᎯ, ᎠᏯ ᏥᏗᏬᏂᎯ,'Ꮩ ᏴᏓ,--?
segments.translation: My son, when he was little, he said, “Just hearing you and my grandma talk, I learned it.” He doesn’t talk as well as we do.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.text: 'Ꮩ ᏴᏓ, “broken Cherokee” ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎰ ᏃᏭ Ꮎ ᎧᎵ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏃᏭ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏲᎩᏬᏂᏌ, just like broken English ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎰ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯ, …but ᏱᏣᏝᏃᎮᏓ,’ᏕᏲ ᎤᏅ,Ꮦ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏙᏳ, ᎧᎵ ᎤᏅ,Ꮤ,

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: A Cherokee—

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭᏭ, ᏳᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎤᏗ ᏯᎩ,ᏛᏛᎭ, ᏱᎦᏪᏍᏗ,
segments.translation: Every once in a while, he struggles to say something, then he’ll ask me how to say it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ, Ꮎ “ᏕᎦᏓᏅᏗᏏᎶ Ꮫ ᎦᏬᏂᎯ,” ᏯᎾᏓ, ᎮᎾ,
segments.translation: And then, the Cherokee, “When he speaks, he’s speaking broken Cherokee,” they’ll say.

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎦᎪ ᏥᎧ-ᏥᎧᏃᎮᏢᎦ ᎠᏭ ᏦᏥᏯᎥ ᎪᎯ Ꮵ-ᏥᏄᏪᏎ
segments.translation: Who was it talking earlier in there? He said something.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I forgot, too.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: “The male.”

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Widagalvtsitlitsu – he said. “It’s gonna go down.”

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: (Both talking)

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: (Both talking)

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᏩᏓᏅ,ᏖᏗ, ᏥᎪᏘᏍᎬ ᏳᏍᏛ ᎧᏃᎮᏗ … ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏞᏍᏗ, ᎤᏠᏱ, ᏱᏂ,ᏥᏫ, ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᏓᏅ,ᏖᏍᎬ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏄᏓᎴᎢ ᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏥᎩ, yeah, ᏱᎦᎯᏃᏎᎸ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎯᏃᎮᎲ ᎨᏍᏗ,--ᎨᏍᏗ, ᏰᎵ ᏯᏃᎵ,Ꭶ, y’know ᏄᏍᏛ ᏂᏪᏍᎬ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩ,Ꮧ’Ꭷ?
segments.translation: In my mind, I could see what he was talking about. But I wouldn’t say the same thing in English. A Cherokee mind is different from a white person’s mind. If you tell them what you’re talking about, they don’t really understand. It’s interesting, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᎾ,ᏚᎵᏍᎬ ᏳᏅᏂ,Ꮧ, ᎩᎳ ᎠᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎩ, … ᎤᏠᏱᏭ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎧᏁᏍᏗ, ᎤᎾ,ᏚᎸᏗ, ᏄᏅᏂ,Ꮧ ᏣᎳᎩ, … ᏴᏓᎭ, ᎡᎵ Ᏹ-Ᏹ-
segments.translation: They want to have what the word is about so they can get the English word close to same in Cherokee. It…

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.translation: It can happen.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵᏍᏓ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎤᎪᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏮᏌ, ᏫᎦᏙᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, … ᏴᏓᎭ ᎡᏍᎦ, ᏄᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ “how would you say this?” – “A Cherokee don’t say that.” They might describe something like that, like if they’re standing back, looking,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎨᏍᏗ, ᎥᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎧᏁᎬ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏳᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎡᎸ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᏓᏅ,ᏖᏗ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎡᎵᏭ ᏯᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥᎦ,
segments.translation: …can happen sometimes, but most of the time, it only works in Cherokee. Sometimes they would say, “How do you say this?” And this bothers the Cherokees, “A Cherokee don’t say that.” They might describe something like that, standing there looking at it. But a Cherokee don’t say that. They need to learn how a Cherokee thinks.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Well, we appreciate it!

segments.speaker: dora-dunn
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: elsie-pritchett
segments.translation: Yeah!
